purpose: Guide a clean, traceable user-story workbook with durable IDs, controlled fields, observable acceptance outcomes, and preserved ingestion provenance.

ordered_sections.title: No.
ordered_sections.purpose: Store a unique, immutable positive-integer identifier as text.

ordered_sections.title: Workstream
ordered_sections.purpose: Classify the story with an approved workstream value.

ordered_sections.title: Feature
ordered_sections.purpose: Name the capability with a concise noun phrase.

ordered_sections.title: As a...
ordered_sections.purpose: Store an approved persona without an article.

ordered_sections.title: I want...
ordered_sections.purpose: State the desired behavior as a concise fragment.

ordered_sections.title: So that...
ordered_sections.purpose: State the intended customer or business outcome as a concise fragment.

ordered_sections.title: Acceptance Criteria
ordered_sections.purpose: Define observable success and applicable boundary, negative, or failure behavior.

ordered_sections.title: Notes
ordered_sections.purpose: Carry traceability, dependencies, evidence, telemetry, or source references when needed.

narrative_rules: Keep each story focused on one persona, one desired behavior, and one outcome.
Store the persona without an article and let the renderer choose the correct article.
Write the desired behavior and outcome as fragments without terminal punctuation.
Use acceptance criteria that describe observable and falsifiable outcomes.
Include negative, boundary, and failure behavior when it applies.
Do not treat visual formatting, hidden rows, strike-through, comments, or undeclared markers as approved semantic truth.
Quarantine incomplete or ambiguous source rows and propose repairs without silently synthesizing content.
evidence_rules: Preserve workbook, sheet, row, visibility, strike, style, formula, displayed value, undeclared columns, and review markers during ingestion.
Keep requirement IDs, dependencies, evidence, telemetry, and source references in Notes when present.
Do not renumber durable story IDs to close gaps.
Do not infer priority, acceptance, deletion, or delivery status from visual state alone.
Do not copy source-specific story facts into a new workbook.
terminology_rules: Use controlled vocabularies for Workstream and persona.
Use only P0, P1, P2, or Decide for Priority.
Keep Feature as a concise noun phrase.
Use one stable term for each actor, behavior, outcome, and referenced requirement.
Treat the normalized tuple of Workstream, Feature, persona, desired behavior, and outcome as the duplicate key.
formatting_rules: Export columns in this exact order: No., Workstream, Feature, As a..., I want..., So that..., Priority, Acceptance Criteria, Notes.
Require columns A through H and include Notes as the optional ninth column.
Use a dark-blue header with white wrapped text.
Top-align and wrap body cells, and emphasize IDs and feature names.
Preserve source column-width intent without copying source-specific data or status colors.
Do not export undeclared review columns in version 1.
hard_fail_rules: Block export when the column schema or order is wrong.
Block export when any required column from A through H is missing.
Block export when an ID is missing, duplicated, mutable, or not positive-integer text.
Block export when a hard duplicate key is present.
Block export when Priority is not P0, P1, P2, or Decide.
Block export when required acceptance criteria are missing or silently synthesized.
Block export when undeclared columns are silently interpreted or included in the version 1 output.
Block export when evidence or source provenance is fabricated or mislabeled.
Block export when source-specific sample facts appear in a new artifact.
Block export when language repair changes story or acceptance meaning.
Block any full-language-conformance status unless the configured bundle, checks, exceptions, and human review are approved.
